haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized. Redis is not called, so no rate-limit counter or budget is used.
haiku-low.q2: Standard: 100 requests per minute total. Counters are per customer ID, so all keys share one budget. Enterprise limit is an open question.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After. The backend never sees that request.
haiku-low.q4: No. A rejected request does not increment the count.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. Counting happens before forwarding, so the request counts even if the backend returns 500.
haiku-low.q6: Fail open: one attempt, no retry. The request is forwarded uncounted, with no X-RateLimit headers, and a ratelimit_store_unavailable metric is emitted.
haiku-low.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: NOT STATED; Product has not decided the limit, so none is set.
haiku-low.q8: One shared Redis holds a counter per customer per minute, key rl:{customerId}:{minute}. Redis deletes each key when its 120 s TTL expires.
haiku-low.q9: Fixed one-minute windows aligned to the UTC clock minute. Each new minute uses a new key, so the count restarts at 0.
haiku-low.q10: The check_and_incr Lua script runs atomically in Redis, and Redis runs one script at a time, so two instances cannot both take the last slot.
haiku-low.q11: Seconds left until the current minute ends, rounded up, with a minimum of 1.
haiku-low.q12: No retry; one attempt with a 50 ms timeout. The client gets the response with no X-RateLimit headers.

sonnet.q1: Gateway returns 401 Unauthorized. Redis is not called, so no counter or budget is affected.
sonnet.q2: They share one budget: counters are keyed by customer ID, not API key. So the total is the plan limit (Standard 100/min); Enterprise limit is NOT STATED (open question).
sonnet.q3: 429 Too Many Requests plus a Retry-After header. The backend never sees the request.
sonnet.q4: No. The count is not incremented on rejection.
sonnet.q5: Yes. Counting happens in check_and_incr before forwarding, so a request that gets a 500 from the backend still counts.
sonnet.q6: Gateway emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric and forwards the request to the backend (fail open). It is not counted, and the response has no X-RateLimit headers.
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100 requests/minute. Enterprise: not decided (open question for Product), so NOT STATED.
sonnet.q8: In one shared Redis used by all 6 gateway instances, one counter per customer per minute with key rl:{customerId}:{minute}. Redis deletes each key when its 120 s TTL expires; nothing else removes them.
sonnet.q9: At the start of each fixed one-minute UTC clock-minute window: a new key is used, so the count starts again at 0.
sonnet.q10: check_and_incr is a single Lua script that Redis runs atomically, one script at a time, so two instances can never both take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: Seconds left until the current minute ends, rounded up, minimum 1.
sonnet.q12: No retry: one attempt with a 50 ms timeout. The client gets the response with no X-RateLimit headers, because the count is unknown.
